strategies.action_description: Front-load the T=1/TOPK<=10 local-slot compaction before GEMM1 and make both GEMM stages consume the same compact local slot arrays. For the fast path, build local_slots, local_experts, token_counts, and local_slot_count first, launch GEMM1 only over the host-known TOPK upper bound with device guards against slot_idx >= local_slot_count[0], and write mid_compact[slot_idx, i] instead of mid[topk_slot, i]. Then pass the same compact slot index to the existing single-token GEMM2 path. Keep GEMM1/GEMM2 arithmetic, FP4 decode helpers, router weights, and fallback paths unchanged; the isolated change is scheduling the local expert work once and reusing it across both GEMMs.
strategies.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: generation 6 selected 6ebb0ad6 as best at 533.856 us, but the current auto baseline is still around 527.168 us for qwen_tp2 T=1. Code evidence in 6ebb0ad6 shows stage1_activation_warp_k_kernel launches over all T*TOPK*I outputs and checks local expert membership inside every warp, while compact_single_token_local_slots_kernel runs only after GEMM1 and therefore only prunes GEMM2. Shape evidence: local_num_experts=256 out of num_experts=512, TOPK=10, so the current GEMM1 launch can spend warp scheduling and topk_id checks on non-local slots that must contribute zero. New L1 evidence: the SM120 MoE data-prep reference outputs compact expert-major maps once for downstream grouped GEMMs, with a single-CTA small-topk path preferred at small topk_length. Inference: the fastest parent has the right compact schedule, but it is used one stage too late. Action: move the schedule boundary before GEMM1 and reuse the compact rows through GEMM2.
strategies.expected_impact: Should reduce useless GEMM1 warp work for non-local top-k routes, remove repeated topk_id/local-range checks from the stage1 hot loop, and make the intermediate layout match the compact single-token GEMM2 path. The gain is shape-dependent: largest when only a subset of TOPK routes are local, neutral when all 10 slots are local.
strategies.risks: If most routed experts are local, the schedule movement may only add one earlier metadata dependency and little speedup. Row mapping mistakes can swap top-k slots, especially because topk_weights must still index the original slot. Keep the parent all-topk GEMM1 path as fallback for T!=1, TOPK>10, or any mismatch.

strategies.action_description: Replace the GEMM2 serial per-thread I-loop with a qwen_tp2-specialized warp-sliced K/I dequant dot. For each active local slot and hidden column, assign one warp to the output, let lanes own disjoint 32-element scale blocks of I=1024, load mid activations and packed FP4 weights with the existing vectorized/cache-policy helpers, accumulate lane-local FP32 partials, then warp-reduce to the same finalize path used by the parent. Keep scheduling, GEMM1, router weighting, and the parent two-column/fallback code unchanged; the category under test is GEMM2 tiled FP4 dequant work partitioning.
strategies.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: 83d98be7 passed at 566.304 us, slower than 6ebb0ad6 but correctness-clean. Code evidence in 83d98be7 shows GEMM2 added adjacent-H two-column reuse, yet each participating thread still walks all gemm2_scale_cols for I=1024 serially inside accumulate_fp4_pair_scaled_i_tiles_gemm2. Prior lineage evidence: GEMM1 warp-sliced K dequant in 06419529 was the first large stable improvement, whereas prior GEMM2 H-tiling and two-column attempts did not split K across lanes. New L1 evidence: the local SM120 NVFP4 split-K/GEMV reports identify small-M long-K work as a parallelism problem, use K-splitting when the serial dot under-fills or has long instruction chains, and require alignment predicates; the vectorized-loads card recommends many lanes per row/dot with 128-bit or wider FP4 loads and cache-policy separation. Inference: GEMM2 still has a serial software-FP4 dequant chain per output. Action: apply the successful warp-sliced K idea to GEMM2 instead of adding more H-column reuse.
strategies.expected_impact: Should shorten the per-thread dequant/FMA chain in GEMM2, improve instruction-level and memory-level parallelism across I scale blocks, and preserve the parent finalization semantics. It is most likely to help when GEMM2 remains visible after GEMM1 warp-slicing.
strategies.risks: One warp per output increases warp count and shuffle overhead, and may be slower if launch occupancy rather than serial K latency is the limit. Restrict the fast path to I_scale_vec==32 and I_scale_cols==32, keep the parent serial/two-column path as fallback, and watch register pressure from per-lane accumulators.

strategies.action_description: Combine the fastest single-token compact schedule with an atomic-free grouped GEMM2 finalize. Keep 6ebb0ad6's GEMM1 and compact local_slots/local_experts path, but change the T=1 GEMM2 kernel to write FP32 slot partials into a compact fixed [TOPK, H] workspace indexed by local slot. Launch a small finalize kernel over H that loops only local_slot_count slots, applies topk_weights and gemm2_bias with the parent semantics, casts directly to bf16, and writes zero when no local slot exists. Do not use the E_local expert_counts/expert_offsets path in this child.
strategies.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: 6ebb0ad6 is the best selected parent at 533.856 us, while sibling 33cb5680 proved an atomic-free partial/finalize idea correctness-clean at 554.112 us but kept the older grouped expert metadata path. Code evidence in 6ebb0ad6 shows the fast T=1 GEMM2 path is compact over TOPK but still uses atomicAdd, __threadfence, completion_counts, out_accum memset, completion_counts memset, and out memset for every active slot/hidden output when expected>1. New L1 evidence: the SM120 split-K GEMV recipe uses a two-phase FP32 partial workspace plus deterministic reduce when extra decomposition is needed, and warns to gate by shape and keep workspace stable; FlashInfer-style grouped finalize keeps router weighting in the epilogue. Inference: the prior atomic-free reducer was structurally sound but paid unnecessary E_local scheduling overhead. Action: reapply only the atomic-free finalize boundary on top of the compact TOPK schedule from 6ebb0ad6.
strategies.expected_impact: Can remove per-output atomics, threadfence, completion-count synchronization, and large zero-initialization traffic from the fastest T=1 path while keeping slot-level GEMM2 parallelism. Expected gain is modest but plausible if completion synchronization is still on the critical path.
strategies.risks: Adds one finalize launch and a [TOPK,H] FP32 workspace, and may lose if GEMM1 dominates or if atomics are hidden behind GEMM2 work. Correctness must preserve duplicate top-k slots, exact local_expert_offset filtering, and gemm2_bias contribution per local route.

evidence_summary: The current profile evidence is CUDA-event evaluator output rather than NCU: qwen_tp2 T=1 passes at 527.168 us in profiles/auto_baseline.json; selected parents pass at 533.856 us (6ebb0ad6), 566.304 us (83d98be7), and 1381.920 us (b1433778). FlashInfer comparison remains BLOCKED because the local flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe worker crashes/errors. Useful arithmetic for T=1,H=4096,I=1024,TOPK=10 is about 251.66 MFLOP, so the best current paths are still below about 0.5 TFLOP/s of useful software-FP4 MoE work. Dominant code evidence: GEMM1 is warp-sliced but still launched over all TOPK before local-slot compaction; GEMM2 still contains serial FP4 dequant loops and atomic completion/finalize synchronization. The strategies therefore target scheduling before GEMM1, K-parallel GEMM2 dequant, and compact atomic-free grouped GEMM2 finalize.
